name: Bitonic vs odd-even merge sort networks
description: Two in-shared-memory sorting networks (a bitonic sort and a Batcher odd-even merge sort) sort the same (key,value) array via different comparator-network topologies, producing the identical permutation.
output_description: CUDA executable writes numeric output to output/cuda_output.txt.

performance.notes: Runtime logs are written by tools/benchmark_case.py.

extraction_notes: Comparator, bitonicSortShared, and oddEvenMergeSortShared reproduced verbatim from NVIDIA/cuda-samples sortingNetworks (bitonicSort.cu, oddEvenMergeSort.cu, sortingNetworks_common.cuh). Host driver, gen_key/gen_val, CMakeLists, and Python oracle are new. Snapshot sk-04.
notes: Real-extraction sorting-network case from collection snapshot sk-04. arrayLength=1024 (single shared-memory block), keys distinct. Output = bitonic kernel's sorted 'key val' pairs, 2048 interleaved integers.
